about: Every shared sync source, the Lean rules in SyncMerge.lean that model its decisions, the conformance tables that hold Swift to them, and what is deliberately not modelled. SyncVerificationCoverageTests fails on a sync source missing from here, an entry for a file that no longer exists, or a rule the model does not define.

Sources/LampCore/LampLibrary.swift.boundary: Only the library's sync paths are modelled: personal import and the deletion ledger. SQLite and filesystem behaviour are assumed.

Sources/LampCore/LampPersonalDeletionLed.boundary: Its item keys are spelled here once, for both clients. Recording a save or a deletion keeps the later time, as `later`.

Sources/LampCore/LampSyncBundleLedgers.s.boundary: The rules both apps follow with the bundle's deletion records: an unreadable personal ledger is skipped where it is read, a contribution joins rather than replaces, and a client with nothing of its own leaves the bundle's as it was. Applying them to a library is each app's.

Sources/LampCore/LampSyncConflict.swift.boundary: Conflict previews and payload encoding are presentation; Swift tests cover the payload round trip.

Sources/LampCore/LampSyncLibraryMigratio.boundary: Which entries are carried, and when the first bundle is written, are held by tables. That the Mac's next pass publishes the library it imported is the Mac's, as is importing it first.

Sources/LampCore/LampSyncSettingsBundleM.boundary: The apps' own settings are opaque and kept as the current copy has them, for each app to merge. An unreadable ledger never stops the merge: of two personal ledgers the readable one stands, and an unreadable deck ledger leaves this copy's, as the passes do.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSharedPreferen.boundary: A field's time is the device's clock, raised past the field it replaces; joining two copies orders by it, then by revision, as `preferenceJoin`.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncArchiveRem.boundary: Reads and decodes an archive an earlier sync left, for the move to per-file sync; nothing publishes one any more. Who kept it and what moves are `earlierLibrary` and `entryFate`, held by LampSyncSettingsStore and LampSyncLibraryMigration.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncBundlePass.boundary: The engine both apps run: it orders core's decisions. Claim before any file, apply what the bundle carries before gathering, downloads and merges before uploads, media before the modules that name it, one bundle update, reaps after it, and a tombstone kept while its file is listed. Each step is decided in core, and the order is held by the `passTrace` table, run through the engine for every combination of work. A client chooses what it plans (`plannedKinds`), while pruning sees the whole listing; a contribution prepared against a bundle that moved is prepared again (`PrepareAgain`), bounded by its attempts; save times reach the plan, so a file saved after its deletion survives; uploads are confirmed through `writeOutcome`, by revision or by reading back, and one never shown back is reported, not recorded. The per-file system model (FilePasses) runs this pass's plan and bundle update across two interleaved devices. A local copy is installed over or deleted only while its digest is the one gathered; a copy made during a pass at a path gathered as absent has nothing to compare with.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncConditiona.boundary: A read-back is compared with the upload by SHA-256 digest, streamed from disk; collision resistance is assumed, as for contentRevision. Which errors count as a refusal is a list of error cases, Swift's. A write may be confirmed by revision alone, waiting while the server still names the revision replaced or a weak tag, for bodies too large to fetch back.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncDirectoryS.boundary: File coordination, NSFileVersion and iCloud's download of an evicted file are the OS's; a timed-out download is an error, never absence. The decision inside the coordinated block is held by tables. iCloud offers no server-side condition, so a later upload from another device can still land after the check. Conflict versions are read and resolved in one coordinated block; which to resolve is the settings store's (`settingsWrite`), and only versions named by their bytes are resolved.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncFilePlan.s.boundary: Gathering the plan's inputs per path and listing each folder is Swift's; the decision for one path, and which revision a listed file is compared by, are held by tables. A path no library deletes is never tombstoned, asked to be deleted here, or reaped; under a tombstone it is planned as a member, and its next write supersedes the tombstone. A write that survives a tombstone carries its time in `supersede`, and is recorded after it. A copy's save time is the caller's to report: one with none loses to any tombstone.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncFileRecord.boundary: Per-source records behind `LampSyncFilePlan.Local`. No record reads as changed, which the plan turns into a download or merge, never an upload over the server's copy. An install records this client's own digest of what it holds, so two clients that encode the same content differently do not trade it for ever. Change is judged by a digest of the bytes every pass, never by size or date.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncFolderLayo.boundary: Path spelling and validation are Swift's. What the plan needs from a path, whether it is media and whether its folder is listed, is the model's FileClass, and filePlanAction's table reaches it through one path of each class.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncFolderPubl.boundary: Only captures a folder the Mac's folder sync left, for the move to per-file sync; nothing publishes a folder any more. A folder whose seal does not vouch for its files is refused.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncJSONCompar.boundary: Classifying a stored string as absent, JSON or text is JSONSerialization's; Swift tests cover it.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncLibraryLay.boundary: Which pass a library gets, straight from the settings store's read.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncLibraryMan.boundary: Revisions compare as tokens here and as numbers in the model; the tables use single-digit revisions, where the two orders agree. Coding, path validation and sorting are Swift's.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncLocalFile..boundary: A local file as the plan reads it, and its digest, read every pass. Each app extends `LampSyncLocalFiles` with its own enumeration; nothing here decides anything.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncRemoteStor.boundary: The provider protocol, and scratch files for bodies streamed to and from disk; no decision of its own. Conditional delete defaults to throwing, so a store that cannot delete fails a reap visibly. `LampSyncVersionedStore` adds reading and resolving a file's conflict versions; a store without it never has any. `readPrefix` reads a file's start, by Range on WebDAV, so an archive is judged without its body.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncSettingsAr.boundary: Where the archive kept the settings database and how a Mac archive carried it, for reading an earlier library and for building archive-era test fixtures; nothing reads or publishes the settings archive over the network any more.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncSettingsBu.boundary: JSON and zlib encoding are Swift's. What the path holds is judged from the unpacked header alone, so an archive is never unpacked to find out it is one.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncSettingsSt.boundary: Reading and the one-HEAD checks are Swift's; the retry and its bound, what an empty path means, which versions merge and what the write does with them are held by tables. `change` and `mergingVersion` must be merges that only compute, which the types cannot enforce. A weak revision is waited out within `patience` before `unversioned`: Apache, which the user's Synology runs, tags a file weak for the second after it changes.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampWebDAVCompatib.boundary: Mapping the phone's WebDAV personal documents to portable records is format conversion; Swift tests cover it.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampWebDAVDirector.boundary: PROPFIND XML parsing; Swift tests cover it.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampWebDAVHTTP.swi.boundary: HTTP request construction; Swift tests cover it.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampWebDAVStorage..boundary: HTTP transport and PROPFIND XML parsing are Swift's; the presence, directory and entity-tag decisions are held by tables. A conditional DELETE sends the PUT's preconditions, so guardedETagCondition holds it too. A PUT that meets a missing folder (409, RFC 4918) makes the folders and is asked once more under the same condition; nothing was written by the first.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampSyncLocalDelet.boundary: What deleting a path from a library removes, called on both sides: whether a removal may be recorded, and whether one recorded elsewhere is carried out. Only the two collection paths, Notes/notes.lamp and Devotionals/devotionals.lamp, are refused; any other notes or writing module, and every highlight set, is a module. The table holds it against several real paths of each kind.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampPortableModule.boundary: Which downloaded module body may replace an installed one: its kind, identity and owner columns, and for a legacy body the columns its import reads. SQLite schema parsing and file integrity are SQLite's; Swift tests cover the inspection.

Sources/LampModuleKit/LampPortableDevoti.boundary: Writing media references and the plain-paragraph shape a writing with no blocks is exported in. JSON parsing is Swift's.
Revising a writing's rich blocks after an edit: block alignment and title matching are Swift's, tested in Swift; which fields survive is modelled.
Projecting a writing's rich blocks for reading and editing; a body is rich only when it carries the block schema and decodes.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Devoti.boundary: Local media files; which media to fetch or upload is core's LampSyncReferencedMedia.
Local devotional rows; their sync decisions are core's (decide, portableImportOutcome) and the iOS module merge.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/ICloud.boundary: Reads only: every iCloud write goes through core's LampSyncDirectoryStore. A read stops on an unresolved NSFileVersion conflict, which the OS must report.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Module.boundary: Local media files for modules; transfer decisions are core's LampSyncReferencedMedia.
The storage protocol each provider adapter implements; it requires readModuleSnapshot and makes no decision of its own.

The phone's module import: SQLite bodies only, inspected by core's LampPortableModuleInspector, replaced inside one write transaction with their registry metadata. Runtime atomicity is SQLite's. Translation JSON import is the person's own, not sync.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/NoteSt.boundary: Local note rows and the conflict record iOS persists; the conflict gate is pendingModuleConflictBlocksExport.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Sync/L.boundary: Design B's pass on the phone: it gathers what the phone holds and carries out LampSyncFilePlan's actions and the pass's one LampSyncSettingsStore.update. The decisions are core's. Every held editable module (notes, writing, highlights), including one held back for an unsettled conflict, reports its save time; installed modules and media have none, by design.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Sync/S.boundary: Provider switching runs through LampSyncBackendTransition; the coordinator's sequencing itself is iOS code held by iOS tests.
The provider protocol: types only, no sync decision.
Shared sync types and errors; no sync decision.
The protocol a syncable record conforms to; no sync decision.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Sync/U.boundary: Serialising settings syncs (one in flight, later requests wait) is Swift concurrency, not modelled.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Sync/W.boundary: Transport; requests and status handling are the shared LampWebDAVStorage's.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Presentatio.boundary: Local deck files; which copy wins is core's LampPresentationDeckPortablePull, held by the deckPull table.

Mirrors decks from the library's deck folder through ModuleStorage on either provider, applies the bundle's deck deletions or failing that the ledger file, and merges images newest-wins; which copy wins is core's LampPresentationDeckPortablePull.

../lamp-bible-macos/Sources/LampBibleMac.boundary: Mac's pass orchestration calls the shared decisions; the byte comparison that settles an undecidable write is settleByBytes.
Shows a set-aside conflict and passes the person's choice to LampLibrary.resolveSyncConflict; the choice itself is core's.
The Mac's half: applying the bundle's deletion records to its library and decks, and reading its own. The rules are core's `LampSyncBundleLedgers`.
`macSettings` has no merge of its own: the newer copy stands. The shared keys go through the preference ledger, which wins where both carry a key.
Sentences for sync errors shown to the person. Core's errors now carry their own descriptions; this decides nothing.

Which module each highlight set is published under, read back from the server's highlight modules' `highlight_meta.id` rather than minted, so a set never gets a second module. A Mac library question; the file-level decisions are the plan's.

Gathers what the Mac holds as `LampSyncFilePlan.Local`: each installed module placed by core's `LampInstalledModuleFile.syncPath()`, never its storage-key filename, and a digest of the bytes on disk. It decides nothing; the plan does (`filePlanAction`).

The Mac's install, merge and removal of single files for its pass, through the same library calls the archive pass made. Merges import by value, and what goes back up is the re-export from the merged library. Record decisions are core's (`decide`, `importOutcome`); the file-level ones are the plan's (`filePlanAction`).
What the person is told before a move or a join. Which one is offered is core's `earlierLibrary`; the move itself is core's `LampSyncLibraryMigration`.

Modules removed on this Mac, written down as they go, for the engine's `Gathered.deletedLocally`. A module leaves no other trace, so without it a removed module is a member nobody holds and is fetched back. What a local deletion becomes, a tombstone and a reap, is the plan's.

When the Mac last saved each collection it publishes, read from its library, for the engine's `Gathered.savedAt`. The decision it feeds, a file saved after its deletion survives, is the plan's (`filePlanAction`).

A write-ahead journal for the settings a pass brings down: staged in the library, applied to UserDefaults, cleared, and replayed at launch and before each pass after a crash. The runtime guarantee depends on the property-list write, the UserDefaults flush and the journal's removal surviving interruption in that order.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Module.boundary: Holds the file records, the deletion ledger, the conflict and publication markers and the provider-switch marker; the decisions about them are the rules named. SQLite durability is assumed.

../lamp-bible-ios/Lamp Bible/Data/Devoti.boundary: How a writing's body is stored: authored Markdown kept for plain drafts, revised blocks for rich sources.

modelOnly.about: Model definitions held to no source, each for a stated reason. SyncVerificationCoverageTests requires every definition in the model to be reached from a source's rules, a conformance table, a system model, or a counterexample listed here.

systemModels.Interleaving: Two devices exchanging whole content against one conditional server: why the per-item rules' being joins makes a sync lose nothing.
systemModels.FilePasses: Two devices running the per-file plan and bundle update, interleaved, checked exhaustively to a bound.

counterexamples.uploadBeforeRead: Why every write is conditioned on the revision it read (staleConditionalWriteRejected).
counterexamples.modificationDateToken: Why a folder revision is a content digest, never a modification date (contentRevision).
counterexamples.earlyBackendWipe: Why a provider switch wipes only after persisting the new provider (deferredBackendWipe).
counterexamples.oldSQLiteReplacementResult: Why the phone retires and copies rows inside one transaction (sqliteReplacementResult).
counterexamples.oldMacHighlightAllowsPublish: Why a failed highlight export stops the publish (macHighlightAllowsPublish).
counterexamples.setForModuleFromTheWholeMapping: Why a highlight module ID is resolved through the sets that exist (setForModule).
